samples: A crisp egg roll gives the table a little punctuation before the first bowl of noodles arrives.
For a table that likes variety, order both styles and compare a bite of each.
A forkful of grilled beef and fine rice noodles tells you more about a vermicelli bowl than its size ever could.
You do not need to mix the whole bowl immediately.
A mound of rice gives grilled pork somewhere to leave its flavor between bites.
Check the variation when placing your order, since the rice choices have different prices.
A spoonful of vegetable broth gives this bowl its starting point before tofu and noodles join the conversation.
Gather a manageable portion of noodles with the tofu instead of lifting a large bundle at once.
The carrot in a spoonful of bò kho changes the bite as much as the beef does.
If you usually order phở, trying bò kho on a later visit gives you a different reference point.
A shrimp changes the pace of a plate of fried rice, giving the next forkful a firmer centerpiece.
If shrimp is what you are looking forward to, the shrimp version keeps the order clear.
One plate can carry three distinct textures without asking you to choose just one of them.
Read the full name when ordering: this particular combination is served with steamed rice.
Pineapple and bell peppers make a plate of chicken change direction from one forkful to the next.
The variations have different prices, so select the version you want when ordering.
Thin strands of green papaya turn a salad into something you gather as much as something you scoop.
That distinction is especially useful if you have a dietary requirement.
A piece of tofu, a little vegetable, and a spoonful of rice let you build the bite yourself.
Keeping some rice separate also gives you room to change the balance as you eat.
